newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Value of Colombian Q1 banana exports up 7.31 pct.
newsitem.headline: Value of Colombian Q1 banana exports up 7.31 pct.

text.p: The value of Colombian banana exports increased 7.31 percent to $111.9 million in the first quarter of 1997, the Colombian Banana Association (Augura) said Friday.

The volume of first-quarter banana exports, however, increased just 0.29 percent to 18.46 million 18.14-kg boxes compared to the same period last year, Jorge Ospina of the association's statistics department told Reuters.

The increase was below levels originally forecast and could lead to a downward revision of the estimates of a year-on-year growth of 5.11 percent in the volume of banana exports and a 5.31 percent gain in their value, Ospina said.

Traditionally the volume of banana production is at its lowest and prices at their highest in the first half of the year. Ospina was unable to say why exports volumes had been lower than expected and said the reasons were still being investigated.

Colombia is the world's third largest banana producer after Ecuador and Costa Rica and had almost 102,010 acres (41,300 hectares) under banana at the end of 1996. The area of banana plantations is expected to increase to more than 103,750 acres (42,000 hectares) by the end of the this year, the association said.
About two-thirds of the production is based in the violence- torn northwest region of Uraba and the remainder around the Caribbean coast port of Santa Marta.
